paragraphs.text: Pontotoc County farmers who suffered drought losses have a new window to apply for federal emergency loans. The U.S. Department of Agriculture named Pontotoc a primary disaster county on Nov. 23. Applications under that designation, S6465, are due July 6, 2027.

The July deadline is separate from a Dec. 7, 2026, deadline that applies to an earlier drought designation. USDA’s April 22 notice included Pontotoc as a neighbor of a designated county. Its November notice lists Pontotoc alongside Chickasaw, Clay, Lee, Monroe and Union as the six primary counties. Producers can ask the Farm Service Agency which designation covers their losses.

The loans can help farms replace essential equipment or livestock, reorganize operations or refinance certain debts. The Farm Service Agency weighs the extent of the losses, what the borrower can offer as collateral and the ability to repay when reviewing an application.

The Pontotoc Farm Service Agency office is at 190 Highway 15 S. in Pontotoc. The USDA service center directory lists 662-489-3563 for that office. Farmers can call there about filing a notice of loss and the deadline for their circumstances.
